MOD Ministers and officials are not obliged to attend or engage with APPG activities. Careful consideration should be given before committing departmental resources. APPG membership can change frequently, and some members might not be MPs or Peers.

There are APPGs on various countries and topics, and those with a defence interest include Armed Forces, Armed Forces Covenant, Defence and Security issues, Drones, Shipbuilding and Repair, and Veterans. They are usually sponsored by industry or other interest groups, which frequently provide a secretariat function to the APPG comprising employees of the sponsoring company. APPG members and their sponsors are listed on the APPG Register on the Parliament website.

Obtain ministerial approval before attending or speaking at any APPG event, including events open to the public. Invitations should not be made through the single Service engagement officers or directly to officials. A formal written invitation (email or letter) must be sent by the APPG to the relevant Minister, via the HCDC Liaison team. Any direct approaches to named officials should be redirected in accordance with this procedure*. The HCDC Liaison team will then send the invitation to the relevant lead branch to request advice and will arrange a response to the APPG.

*The only exceptions to this process are invitations from the Armed Forces APPG which can be dealt with via the visits approvals process (Section 15) for Ministerial approval.

Any invitation to speak at an APPG event or to brief an APPG must be treated in the same way as an invitation to speak at a public event. Once Ministerial approval has been given, speeches or briefings must be submitted for formal authorisation under the terms of the 2026 Contact with the Media DIN.

Miscellaneous

Other government departments

Obtain approval from the relevant MOD minister before briefing another government minister, whether verbally or in writing. Obtain approval from the Secretary of State’s Office before briefing Cabinet ministers.

OGDs may contact MOD teams directly asking for inputs into Parliamentary Questions or Ministerial Correspondence. All such requests should be directed through the Parliamentary Branch.

Routine cross-government functions, such as the Home Office Royal and Ministerial Visits Team that support Ministerial overseas visits, do not need approval where the relevant private office is already involved. If contacted unexpectedly by one of these teams, Parliamentary Branch can provide advice and identify the appropriate point of contact.

Political Activity

Any visits made by parliamentarians must take place on the understanding that they cannot be used for political purposes. Commanding Officers and heads of establishment must be impartial in their dealings with all parties.

Parliamentary or Assembly Candidates during an Election Period

When a Parliament or Assembly is dissolved, its members cease to be MPs or MDLs (Scottish, Welsh and Northern Ireland representatives) and are treated as any other member of the public, with the exception of Ministers who retain their role during this time. Candidates seeking election, from all parties, are treated as members of the public and are not to be afforded any treatment over and above that generally available to members of the public until they become elected. The Permanent Secretary’s office will promulgate Cabinet Office Election Guidance to the Department.

Members of the House of Lords remain so following the dissolution Parliament and so visits involving active Peers should continue to follow the guidance above. Committees of the House of Lords do not function during the dissolution period so any planned visits should be postponed.

At the discretion of the commanding officer, election candidates are permitted to visit Service Family Accommodation situated inside defence establishments, to canvass Service personnel and their families or to take electors to the polling stations. Canvassing in Single Living Accommodation (SLA) is not permitted. If a candidate requests permission to canvass Service personnel living inside a defence establishment, then, at the discretion of the Commanding Officer, a communal space within the establishment may be made available to allow Service personnel (particularly those living in SLA) who wish to hear the candidate to do so. Commanding Officers, taking operational and security considerations into account, are to ensure that no bias is shown for or against any political party that makes such a request.

If one party or candidate is granted a facility, then all other parties or candidates asking for the same would have to be granted the same facility. Where permission to visit a Service establishment is granted, it is to be made clear to the candidate that the visit may take place only on the condition that no members of the Armed Forces are to be used for political advantage; there will be no media involvement, nor should the visit be used to generate any publicity including use of private images and/or quotes on promotional material or websites. Service personnel whose duties do not preclude them from attending a meeting with a candidate should be allowed to do so. Uniform should not be worn unless otherwise unavoidable.

Any correspondence from candidates, constituency parties or other party bodies with requests to visit defence establishments other than Service Family Accommodation should be forwarded through the appropriate MOD Secretariat for a response. The originator should be informed that Ministerial approval is being sought. Cabinet Office provides guidance on elections, so please contact the Permanent Secretary’s office for any further guidance required.

MPs and MDLs can make confidential enquiries with officials or a government minister on behalf of MOD personnel. MPs and MDLs represent all the people in their local area, whether they voted for them or not; the local MP and/or MDL should always be contacted first to raise an issue at Parliament.

Personnel should consider whether contacting their constituency parliamentarian is the most appropriate way to resolve a workplace concern. Where possible, concerns should first be raised through the chain of command, line management or other internal processes. Personnel may also wish to contact an HR or welfare representative for advice

Raising a concern or whistleblowing

Personnel who raise a concern or make a whistleblowing disclosure through parliamentary channels other than their constituency parliamentarian are not acting on behalf of the MOD and do not need prior authorisation under this DIN. However, personnel must consult the Raising a Concern policy in JSP 492 (internal access only). This guidance explains:

how to raise a concern

when legal protection may apply under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 (PIDA)

what constitutes a protected disclosure under PIDA or MOD policy

Although prior authorisation is not required, disciplinary action may still be taken where a disclosure is not considered to be a protected disclosure.

Parliamentarians visiting defence establishments

Approval must be obtained through defence ministers before any visit takes place. Submit visit approval requests through the chain of command to the relevant MOD Secretariat, which will formally submit the request through the Ministers’ Office.

Non-MOD organisations operating from the Defence Estate may invite parliamentarians to visit sites without requiring an approval to be submitted. Such visits must however be notified to the Service or Defence organisation in command of the site in advance of invitations being sent, which in turn must notify the relevant MOD Secretariat as soon as possible.

Constituency representatives

The exception to the above (Parliamentarians visiting defence establishments) is that parliamentarians may visit Defence establishments within their constituency (or a bordering one) without prior approval, although the relevant MOD Secretariat/Service point of contact must still be informed. Visits should have no media involvement.

Where a visit may highlight sensitive issues, the relevant MOD Secretariat should determine whether ministerial approval is required. MOD Secretariats should ensure that they seek Ministerial approval with at least two weeks’ notice wherever possible.

You must obtain ministerial approval before involving the media. Clearly identify all media involvement in the approval request submitted to the minister.

Visits to Cadet Force establishments which are not located on a Defence establishment have separate regulations in JSP 814, Chapter 7 (internal access only).

Permission is not required for any visits related to Armed Forces’ Day or Remembrance Sunday events, or other civic events such as (but not limited to) Freedom of City, Twinning or Festival days.

Where a parliamentarian requires regular access to an establishment, for example as a Regimental Honorary Colonel, arrange a longer-term agreement through the Ministers’ Office via the relevant MOD Secretariat.

Parliamentarians’ office staff are not permitted to visit Defence establishments as they are not elected representatives. This does not apply to clerks of committees who hold a specified apolitical role within Parliament and are expected to accompany visits in support of their committee (but not entitled to undertake visits in their own right) but does apply to APPG staff as they have no formal role.

Security

Parliamentarians visiting Defence establishments must always be escorted. As visitors to a site, parliamentarians must always comply with site/unit security rules, including rules relating to personal electronic devices and the taking/sharing of photographs/videos/recordings.

Travel expenses

Parliamentarians are not entitled to travel and accommodation at the MOD’s expense. They should arrange and pay for their own travel to and from establishments and be charged non-entitled rates for use of Service accommodation. This also applies to members of the HCDC and any other parliamentary committee members. As an exception, Opposition party leaders and Defence spokespersons may travel on Service transport and stay in Service accommodation free of charge when visiting UK Armed Forces deployed on operations.

Invitations to events

Seek advice from the relevant MOD Secretariat before inviting a parliamentarian to an MOD or service event. Attendance may not be appropriate for political or other reasons. The Secretariat will advise accordingly. You may also need advice from Parliamentary Branch or the Minister’s Office for high-profile or politically sensitive events. Do not issue invitations until ministerial approval has been granted.

Secretariats may wish to consider whether a Ministerial submission may be appropriate for some high profile or politically sensitive events where the Minister may require more detailed advice and information than can be provided within the approval request. You should confirm this with the relevant Ministerial Office before providing the submission.
